content.text: **Year opened:** The facility was opened in autumn 2006. An upstreamNet factsheet says the On Demand Data Center was launched after IBM acquired it that autumn,

citations.cited_text: The On Demand Data Center (ODC21) was opened after being acquired by IBM in the fall of 2006 with an area of 770.

content.text: The On Demand Data Center (ODC21) was opened after being acquired by IBM in the fall of 2006 with an area of 770.
**Size (white space):** The operator-side factsheet puts the built-out data centre space at roughly 3,000 m². Its 2025 version lists

citations.cited_text:
**Facts:**

| ▪  | Built-out data center area: approx. 3.000 square metres  |
| --- | --- |
| ▪  | Infrastructure technical area: 1.560 square metres ...

content.text: built-out data center area: approx. 3.000 square metres; Infrastructure technical area: 1.560 square metres; Side rooms, reception and offices: 600 square metres

. I used the 3,000 m² figure because it is the data hall area, and no gross floor area is given by the operator.

**Size (other figures):** A directory lists a

citations.cited_text: The building ODC21 (IBM colocation site) sits in has a footprint of 66,090 sq ft, which is about 6,140 square meters.
citations.title: ODC21 (IBM colocation site) Data Center in Vienna

content.text: footprint of 66,090 sq ft, which is about 6,140 square meters.

This is a building footprint, not a gross floor area, and it comes from a third-party directory, so I did not use it as the primary value.

**Caveats:** The factsheets are published by upstreamNet, which provides colocation services at the site, not by IBM itself. IBM's own website did not give any data on this facility. The 2006 date refers to the site's opening under IBM ownership, not to a later expansion. The 2009 expansion added only 230 m² in the main building and 350 m² in a neighbouring building for emergency workstations.
